cass: Quick bring-up for Aurora-13B compact quant runs. Tested fp16 / int8 / int6 across slices: long-form summarization (N=220), multi-turn retrieval QA (N=150), short assistant chat (N=280). Main takeaway: int6 is the pragmatic sweet spot; int4-like aggressive configs save cost but have reproducible compression on procedural tasks.

omar: can you paste the tiny scorecard + deltas so GTN/PM can get a sense?

cass: short table (aggregated): ROUGE-L / Accuracy@1 (retrieval QA) / p50 latency@1024 / est cost($/1k tokens)

cass: ```
variant | ROUGE-L | Acc@1 | p50 ms | cost($/1k)
fp16    | 0.748   | 0.86  | 160    | 1.00
int8    | 0.741   | 0.85  | 125    | 0.68
int6    | 0.736   | 0.843 | 105    | 0.57
int4(agg)| 0.715  | 0.81  | 85     | 0.40

delta int6 vs fp16: -1.6% ROUGE-L, -1.9pp Acc@1, -34% p50, -43% cost
delta int4 vs fp16: -4.4% ROUGE-L, -5.0pp Acc@1, -47% p50, -60% cost
```

yvette: ok. where do we see the failures for int4/int6 specifically?

cass: triage notes: int6 regressions are mostly: shorter intermediate reasoning steps (55%), slight numeric drift (25%), tone concision (20%). int4 adds: missing steps that change correctness (60%), hallucinated entities (25%), stop/truncation artifacts (15%). Short chat (<128 tokens) is stable across int8/int6.

omar: tails? 95/99p?

cass: 95p: fp16 400ms, int8 310ms, int6 270ms, int4 230ms. 99p: fp16 760ms, int6 520ms, int4 470ms. So tails tighten with lower memory footprint and better packing.

yvette: recommended routing policy for GTN? simple rules please.

cass: proposal (lean):
- Default: aurora-13b-int6 for general API/web traffic.
- Route to fp16 when input_tokens > 600 OR request_tag == "high_recall" OR route == "legal/financial".
- Use int4 only for pre-processed internal batch summarization jobs with manual audits.

cass: config snippet: ```json
{"routing": {"default_model": "aurora-13b-int6", "rules": [{"match": {"input_tokens_gt": 600}, "model": "aurora-13b-fp16"}, {"match": {"request_tag": "high_recall"}, "model": "aurora-13b-fp16"}]}}
```

omar: rollout gates? what should we set as the acceptance criteria?

cass: propose:
- Accept int6 if ROUGE-L drop <= 2% absolute on long-doc holdout AND Acc@1 drop <= 2pp AND hallucination increase <= 3pp.
- Block int4 from any high-recall route. int4 requires 72h shadow + manual audit and vendor runtime validation.

yvette: ops notes: int6 kernel available on standard fleets, int4 uses third-party runtime we need to validate on dedicated pools. Recommend canary 3% traffic for int6 + full shadowing and 1% start for int4 with 72h shadow + manual samples. Add auto-eval hooks for ROUGE/Acc/hallucination that fail rollout.

omar: econ sketch for the pricing slide? rough monthly impact if we route 75% traffic to int6.

cass: back-of-envelope: baseline all fp16 = $130k/month. With 75% int6, 20% int8, 5% fp16 => ~$90k/month (~31% savings). If we offload 10% of batch to int4 (internal only) incremental estimate drops to ~$82k/month but risk buffer -> plan ~$95k/month.

yvette: product/GTN will want a tiny forecast table for Q next quarter. can you post that as a slide?

cass: will prepare a 2-slide deck: (1) scorecard + routing recs (2) 3-scenario econ forecast (conservative/expected/optimistic). Will attach link in this thread.

omar: pls ensure the canary includes automatic hallucination checks and a holdout set for retrieval QA precision. we'll gate any rollout on those checks.

ci-bot: Canary created: canary/aurora-int6-2024-10-02 (traffic 3%). See /deploys/9987

yvette: thanks all. i'll coordinate infra validation for int4 runtime and schedule a GTN review after 48h metrics.

cass: filing follow-up thread when 48h snapshot is ready. :thumbsup:
